taxes.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","action":"promised austerity-based budget reallocation","mechanism":"reorienting public resources from current spending to investment while not raising taxes","outcome":"intended a more investment-heavy budget mix without new taxes","dates":["2018"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"la \"austeridad republicana\", para reorientar los recursos públicos de los gastos corrientes a la inversión sin subir los impuestos;","locator":"extracted HTML block 5","attribution":"CIDOB political biography","period_fit":"2018 campaign platform","source_limitations":["Campaign promise, not evidence of implementation.","Retrospective biographical source with editorial framing."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["The claim, date, mechanism, and attribution are supported by the cited unit."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"The 2018 campaign platform promised to fight poverty and raise human development for vulnerable groups.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","action":"promised a social-development agenda","mechanism":"addressing social causes by fighting poverty and raising human development among vulnerable groups","outcome":"intended to raise human development among vulnerable groups","dates":["2018"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"la atención de las \"causas sociales\", combatiendo la pobreza y elevando el desarrollo humano de los colectivos vulnerables","locator":"extracted HTML block 5","attribution":"CIDOB political biography","period_fit":"2018 campaign platform","source_limitations":["Campaign promise, not evidence of implementation.","Retrospective biographical source with editorial framing."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Replaced the broader outcome about better conditions with the passage's specific human-development commitment."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"The 2018 campaign platform promised to raise domestic gasoline supply to reduce imports and prices and to pursue energy and food self-sufficiency, including guaranteed prices for local agricultural producers.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","action":"promised supply-side energy and food policies","mechanism":"expanding domestic gasoline supply and offering guaranteed prices to local agricultural producers","outcome":"intended to reduce gasoline imports and prices and promote energy and food self-sufficiency","dates":["2018"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"el aumento de la oferta de gasolina autóctona para reducir las importaciones y rebajar precios; las autosuficiencias energética y alimentaria, en el caso del agro ofreciendo a los productores locales precios de garantía;","locator":"extracted HTML block 5","attribution":"CIDOB political biography","period_fit":"2018 campaign platform","source_limitations":["Campaign promise, not evidence of implementation.","Retrospective biographical source with editorial framing."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Clarified that guaranteed prices applied to local agricultural producers and retained the passage's prospective status."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"CIDOB characterized the 2018-2024 platform as accepting free-market orthodoxy, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, and a floating peso while rejecting privatization and foreign ownership trends in strategic sectors and prioritizing national production.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"context","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","action":"defined his governing platform","mechanism":"combining orthodox macroeconomic principles with opposition to privatization and foreign ownership trends in strategic sectors","outcome":"CIDOB characterized the platform as a pragmatic social-democratic orientation","dates":["2018-2024"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"su plataforma para el período de gobierno 2018-2024 sugiere una socialdemocracia pragmática que asume las nociones ortodoxas del libre mercado, la estabilidad macroeconómica, la disciplina presupuestaria y la flotación del peso, conjugadas, eso sí, con el rechazo a las \"tendencias privatizadoras\" y la \"extranjerización\" de sectores estratégicos, y la prioridad para la \"producción nacional\".","locator":"extracted HTML block 6","attribution":"CIDOB political biography","period_fit":"2018-2024 governing platform","source_limitations":["Editorial retrospective description, not a formal policy document.","Describes a platform rather than executed policy."],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Attributed the interpretive characterization explicitly to CIDOB.","Replaced the broader wording about limits on privatization and foreign ownership with the passage's opposition to those trends."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"During López Obrador's DF administration, the city experienced a public-works campaign and several social-protection programs, most prominently the Universal Food Pension for Older Adults, while the municipal government resisted implementing Seguro Popular.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador and the DF municipal government","action":"pursued public works and social-protection programs while resisting Seguro Popular","mechanism":"urban infrastructure works and municipal social-protection programs","outcome":"CIDOB reports that residents benefited from social programs, including the pension for older adults","dates":["2000-2005"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Por un lado, el DF conoció una vigorosa campaña de obras públicas para la mejora y ampliación de una serie de infraestructuras urbanas. Por otro lado, los mexiqueños se beneficiaron de varios programas de protección social, el más destacado de los cuales fue la Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores. El Gobierno municipal se resistió a implementar el Seguro Popular, aprobado por el Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS) y basado en la aportación de cuotas por los beneficiarios, aduciendo que los defeños ya recibían de sus instituciones municipales la necesaria cobertura social y además gratuita.","locator":"extracted HTML block 21","attribution":"CIDOB political biography","period_fit":"2000-2005 Mexico City governorship","source_limitations":["Retrospective narrative; the passage mixes description and evaluation.","Does not quantify infrastructure improvement or social-program outputs."],"question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Changed observed_fact to source_assertion because this is a retrospective biographical account.","Removed the unsupported conclusion that infrastructure improved; the passage establishes a campaign intended to improve and expand infrastructure.","Changed polarity to mixed to reflect the simultaneous refusal to implement Seguro Popular."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In its account of supporters' views of López Obrador's DF governorship, CIDOB identified his commitment to regular accountability, transparency, and participatory democracy as a point in his favor.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","action":"was described as committed to accountability-oriented norms","mechanism":"regular accountability, transparency, and participatory democracy","outcome":"CIDOB reports a favorable assessment attributed to his supporters","dates":["2000-2005"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Otro punto a su favor era su compromiso con la rendición regular de cuentas, la transparencia y la democracia participativa.","locator":"extracted HTML block 19","attribution":"CIDOB political biography, within its account of supporters' views","period_fit":"2000-2005 Mexico City governorship","source_limitations":["Value judgment presented within the biography's account of supporters' views.","A reported commitment does not establish implementation or results."],"question_ids":["5B.7"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Corrected the attribution to preserve the surrounding passage's explicit framing as the view of supporters and partisans."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"The 2006 platform called for fighting tax fraud and evasion, sharply cutting current spending, halving the president's salary, and having a truth commission investigate FOBAPROA's activities.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","action":"set tax-compliance, austerity, and investigation proposals in the campaign platform","mechanism":"current-spending cuts, tax-compliance enforcement, and a truth commission for FOBAPROA","outcome":"intended lower current spending and an investigation of FOBAPROA's activities","dates":["2006"],"quantities":["half the president's salary"],"excerpt":"A la vez, urgía combatir el fraude y la evasión fiscal, así como recortar drásticamente los gastos corrientes, siendo el primer paso la reducción a la mitad del sueldo del presidente de la República. En cuanto a las actividades del FOBAPROA, serían investigadas por una Comisión de la Verdad.","locator":"extracted HTML block 30","attribution":"CIDOB political biography","period_fit":"2006 campaign platform","source_limitations":["Campaign platform text, not downstream spending or audit evidence.","Truth-commission language indicates intent, not a completed investigation."],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.7"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Removed the broader characterization of the platform as anti-corruption and accountability-focused because the excerpt specifically supports tax compliance, spending cuts, and a proposed investigation."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"IMF staff estimated that retail fuel price stabilization in 2022 lowered inflation by 2 percentage points, cost around 1.5% of GDP, and disproportionately benefited higher-income households.","claim_type":"interpretation","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"used retail fuel-price stabilization to mitigate cost pressures","mechanism":"retail fuel-price stabilization","outcome":"lower estimated inflation alongside a sizable budget cost and disproportionately greater benefits for higher-income households","dates":["2022"],"quantities":["2 percentage points","around 1.5 percent of GDP"],"excerpt":"• Retail fuel price stabilization has directly reduced cost pressures, lowering inflation by an estimated 2 percentage points this year. The measure has come at a sizeable budgetary cost, estimated at around 1.5 percent of GDP, and has disproportionately benefited higher income households. Furthermore, by diluting price signals, the policy has short-circuited the desirable adjustment in fuel demand.","locator":"page 19","attribution":"IMF staff, IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"2022 inflation-shock response","source_limitations":["IMF staff estimate, not an administrative microdata audit.","Distributional incidence is described qualitatively and may be model-based."],"question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Corrected source_id from IMF-010 to the packet's exact identifier, MAC-010.","Made IMF staff attribution explicit and removed the unsupported mechanism wording 'fuel subsidies and price smoothing' in favor of the passage's term."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The 2022 PACIC package centered on fuel subsidies expected to cost MEX$395.4 billion, or 1.4% of GDP, and its food-price measures largely used preexisting agricultural programs plus an agreement with major retailers to limit price increases for 24 core food items.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"launched anti-inflation household measures","mechanism":"fuel subsidies, preexisting agricultural support programs, and a retailer price agreement","outcome":"the passage describes the package's composition and expected federal budget cost","dates":["2022"],"quantities":["MEX$395.4 billion","1.4 percent of GDP","24 core food items"],"excerpt":"Fuel subsidies lie at the heart of PACIC and are expected to cost the Federal government around MEX$395.4 billion (1.4 percent of GDP) by the end the year. Meanwhile, efforts to contain rising food costs have largely sought to leverage pre-existing agricultural support programs but also include an agreement with major retailers to limit prices increases for 24 core food items at no cost to the Federal government.","locator":"page 74","attribution":"IMF staff, IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"2022 household inflation-response package","source_limitations":["IMF staff summary of the authorities' 2022 package; not all measures are quantified here.","The passage does not establish the package's effects on household budgets or actual food-price outcomes."],"question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Corrected source_id from IMF-010 to MAC-010.","Removed the unsupported outcome that the measures supported household budgets and restrained food-price increases.","Changed observed_fact to source_assertion because the cost is an expectation reported by IMF staff."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The 2023 draft budget increased planned expenditure by 8.5% nominally relative to the authorities' estimated 2022 outturn, accommodating higher interest payments, social pensions, priority infrastructure, and modest increases for specified rural programs, while making no tax-code change and continuing anti-evasion and avoidance efforts.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"context","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"prepared the 2023 draft budget","mechanism":"higher planned expenditure on interest, social programs, infrastructure, and rural supports with no tax-code change","outcome":"specified proposed budget allocations and continued tax-compliance efforts","dates":["2023"],"quantities":["8.5 percent","0.1 percentage points of authorities' projected GDP"],"excerpt":"Compared to the authorities estimated 2022 outturn, expenditure in 2023 is increased by 8.5 percent in nominal terms (or by 0.1 percentage points of authorities’ projected GDP). This increase accommodates higher spending of interest payments, some social programs—particularly (non-contributory) social pensions for the elderly—and priority infrastructure projects. In addition, the allotted funding for social programs related to fertilizers, procurement of national milk, and rural supplies has also been increased, though the size of the programs remains modest. On the revenue side, the budget entails no change in the tax code but highlights continued efforts to reduce tax evasion and avoidance.","locator":"page 13","attribution":"IMF staff, IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"2023 draft budget assessed in late 2022","source_limitations":["Staff report summarizes the 2023 draft budget rather than year-end outturn.","This is a proposed budget, not realized execution."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Corrected source_id from IMF-010 to MAC-010.","Removed October 18, 2022 because that is the staff report's completion date, not a date supplied for the budget action in this excerpt.","Removed the unsupported favorable outcome and neutral-fiscal-stance language.","Changed observed_fact to source_assertion and polarity to context to preserve the proposal's prospective status."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"In April 2021, Mexico enacted legislation restricting workforce subcontracting with the stated aim of preventing labor-law violations and tax evasion; it also tightened registration and reporting requirements and made non-compliance a criminal offence.","claim_type":"legal_status","polarity":"context","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"enacted subcontracting restrictions","mechanism":"restricting third-party management of workers and tightening registration and reporting requirements","outcome":"established legal restrictions and criminal liability for non-compliance","dates":["April 2021"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"In April 2021, the authorities enacted new legislation restricting the subcontracting of the workforce, with the aim of preventing the violation of labor law and tax evasion. The new law bans service firms from providing employees to be supervised and managed by a third-party, while it still allows subcontracting of services if the employees are monitored by the firm providing the service.1 The legislation also tightened registration and reporting requirements. Non-compliance with this new subcontracting law became a criminal offence.","locator":"page 69","attribution":"IMF staff, IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"April 2021 labor-law reform","source_limitations":["Describes the law's enactment and stated purpose, not its effectiveness in preventing violations or evasion.","Legal status does not by itself show enforcement quality or incidence."],"question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.8"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Corrected source_id from IMF-010 to MAC-010.","Changed claim_type to legal_status and polarity to context.","Replaced the unsupported achieved outcome 'curbed outsourcing abuse' with the law's stated aim and legal effects."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"IMF staff reported that Mexico approved a new electricity law that replaced auctions with nonmarket-based policies, gave regulatory power to CFE, and created conflicts of interest and disrupted contracts signed under the 2013 reform.","claim_type":"interpretation","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"changed electricity-market rules","mechanism":"replacing auctions with nonmarket-based policies and giving regulatory power to the state-owned CFE","outcome":"IMF staff assessed that the change created conflicts of interest and disrupted contracts signed under the 2013 reform","dates":["2013"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"A new electricity law, however, was approved and has replaced auctions by nonmarket-based policies, with regulatory power given to the Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE), the state-owned electricity company. This has created conflicts of interest and disrupted contracts signed under the 2013 reform.","locator":"page 33","attribution":"IMF staff, IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"electricity-policy assessment published in 2022","source_limitations":["IMF staff characterization of the energy-law shift; it does not independently adjudicate legality.","The excerpt does not state the enactment date of the new electricity law."],"question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Corrected source_id from IMF-010 to MAC-010.","Removed 2022 as the law's date because the excerpt does not supply it.","Changed claim_type from observed_fact to interpretation and attributed the assessed consequences explicitly to IMF staff."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"LAW-005","claim":"The 8 December 2022 fuel-stimulus notice set reduced excise support for gasoline and diesel for 10-16 December 2022, with gasoline under 91 octanes and diesel receiving nonzero subsidies and premium gasoline receiving none.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"Mexican fiscal authorities","action":"published a fuel-stimulus schedule","mechanism":"setting lower excise rates and per-liter stimulus amounts for selected fuels","outcome":"temporarily reduced fuel taxes for the specified week","dates":["December 8, 2022","December 10-16, 2022"],"quantities":["26.96%","59.77%","$1.4803","$3.6071","$4.0114","$4.6375"],"excerpt":"Artículo Primero. Los porcentajes del estímulo fiscal para el periodo comprendido del 10 al 16 de diciembre de 2022, aplicables a los combustibles automotrices son los siguientes: Combustible Porcentaje de Estímulo Gasolina menor a 91 octanos 26.96% Gasolina mayor o igual a 91 octanos y combustibles no fósiles 0.00% Diésel 59.77% Artículo Segundo. Los montos del estímulo fiscal para el periodo comprendido del 10 al 16 de diciembre de 2022, aplicables a los combustibles automotrices son los siguientes: Combustible Monto del estímulo fiscal (pesos/litro) Gasolina menor a 91 octanos $1.4803 Gasolina mayor o igual a 91 octanos y combustibles no fósiles $0.0000 Diésel $3.6071","locator":"extracted HTML block 2","attribution":"Acuerdo 173/2022, Diario Oficial de la Federación","period_fit":"December 10-16, 2022 fuel-stimulus schedule","source_limitations":["Official notice gives rates and effective period but not downstream pass-through or household incidence.","It is a legal schedule, not a performance evaluation."],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"verification_status":"rejected","verification_notes":["The excerpt is not a single contiguous substring of extracted HTML block 2: it prepends Article One wording from the preceding unit and compresses intervening line breaks and table text.","The quantities $4.0114 and $4.6375 are not contained in the supplied excerpt.","The outcome that taxes were reduced is an inference from the legal schedule; the notice establishes rates and stimulus amounts but not downstream incidence.","The candidate cannot be split because the instruction prohibits adding new candidates."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"In its 2022 surveillance materials, the IMF stated that Mexico had timely, comprehensive economic data adequate for surveillance and subscribed to the SDDS.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexico","action":"provided macroeconomic data and subscribed to the SDDS","mechanism":"timely availability of comprehensive economic data and participation in the SDDS","outcome":"the IMF considered the data adequate for surveillance","dates":["2022"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Mexico has accepted the obligations of Article VIII, sections 2, 3, and 4. Comprehensive economic data are available for Mexico on a timely basis and economic data are adequate for surveillance. It subscribes to the SDDS.","locator":"page 97","attribution":"IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation), Informational Annex","period_fit":"2022 IMF surveillance and data-adequacy assessment","source_limitations":["Institutional IMF data-quality assessment, not evidence of López Obrador's personal choices.","Country-level assessment only."],"question_ids":["5B.7"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Corrected source_id from IMF-010 to MAC-010.","Corrected the mandatory locator from page 98 to page 97, where the exact excerpt appears.","Changed actor from Mexican authorities to Mexico and claim_type from observed_fact to source_assertion to reflect an IMF assessment."],"premium_verification_required":false}],"rejected_or_omitted_passages":["Omitted long biographical passages on family background, early career, and electoral history that did not add new 5B evidence beyond the platform and governing episodes captured above.","Omitted repeated IMF tables and charts that restated the same macroeconomic and fiscal facts already captured in narrative passages.","Rejected the LAW-005 candidate because its purported exact excerpt is assembled across units rather than being a contiguous substring of the cited unit, and two listed quantities do not appear in that excerpt."],"unresolved_gaps":["No direct packet evidence on how economic officials were appointed, retained, or replaced on the basis of performance versus loyalty (5B.2).","The packet contains mostly campaign statements, IMF staff assessments, and legal notices rather than independent audit-level verification of every implementation effect.","The packet identifies the IMF source as MAC-010, whereas all draft IMF candidates used the unsupported identifier IMF-010; those identifiers were corrected.","The packet does not state the enactment date of the electricity law in the cited passage, so only the 2013 contract-reform reference remains as a claim date."]}
